rationale: Amendment 3 changes UNB S001 to UNOC only with effect from 1 November 2026. On 30 October the agreed syntax identifier is still UNOA (section 3), so the sender's UNOC interchanges, sent since 28 October, use a syntax identifier that is not yet agreed, and the receiver's CONTRL rejects them at UNB. The receiver is behaving as agreed and the agreement is consistent; the sender switched four days early and must send UNOA until 1 November. That the content is plain ASCII does not matter: the declared syntax identifier is what the receiver checks. Only S001 0001 must change; the version (0002) is 3 under both.
